text:
maya: Heads up — customers are seeing 503s when our routing falls back to a smaller quantized model. They read it as a service outage, but its actually an intentional graceful fallback. Can we surface something clearer?

samir: Ugh, thats bad. 503 implies server error. We should avoid returning 5xx for expected degradations. Options: 200 + flag, a newer 2xx/3xx, or a more specific 4xx. Each has client UX tradeoffs.

devon: We need to separate terminal failures (actual infra/errors) from soft degradations (fallbacks). Proposal: preserve non-200 for terminal errors. For fallback, return 200 but include structured headers + telemetry that indicate "outcome=fallback" and a small body field describing quality. That keeps HTTP semantics for success but surfaces machine-readable signals.

alyssa: Concern: many clients auto-retry on 5xx. If we switch to 200 for fallback, retries will stop (which might be desired). But some SDKs treat non-200 as critical. Maybe also add header `X-Redwood-Outcome: fallback` and `X-Redwood-Retry-Suggest: false` so SDKs can decide.

samir: Another thought: send 200 + `X-Redwood-Outcome` + `Retry-After` when it's transient capacity pressure (so clients can back off or failover). 206 Partial Content is tempting but semantically weird for generation APIs.

maya: For customer-facing console copy we should be explicit: "Partial capacity — using reduced-cost fallback model. API call succeeded but output quality may be degraded." Need short, non-technical phrasing for the badge/modal. @devon can you draft?

devon: Drafting header/body examples now. Quick sample headers:
```
X-Redwood-Outcome: fallback
X-Redwood-Fallback-Model: redwood-3b-quant
X-Redwood-Fallback-Quality: warn
```
and body snippet:
```
{"status":"ok","outcome":"fallback","fallback_model":"redwood-3b-quant","quality_score":0.72}
```
This preserves success semantics but gives machine-readable info.

alyssa: Telemetry needs to capture this: event `inference.outcome` with tags outcome=fallback/model_id/quality_bucket, and a metric `fallback.count` per route/model. Also add a sample rate so we don't overload metrics.

maya: SDK impact: we need an SDK story. Header-first approach reduces breakage: emit headers behind a FF, then SDKs read header and surface user-friendly event "fallback used" instead of treating as error. I can own the SDK spec.

samir: Proposed rollout: 1) header + telemetry behind feature-flag at routing layer (no body changes). 2) console UX: badge + modal copy (show fallback model + quality score). 3) SDK update to parse header and expose outcome/shouldRetry. 4) if adoption ok after 2-3 weeks, evaluate changing body semantics (opt-in) for certain routes.

devon: Console UX idea: show a small orange pill "Fallback in use" next to response breakdown with link to runbook and suggestions (upgrade plan, reserved capacity). Modal copy: "We're using a lower-capacity model to keep your app responsive. Results may be less accurate. Learn how to avoid fallbacks."

deploy-bot: canary deployed to eu-west-1 with header emission enabled for feature flag `fallback-headers` (canary 2% traffic) :rocket:

maya: Action items: devon to draft a short RFC by EOD (headers + body example + telemetry schema), samir to implement header emission behind `fallback-headers`, alyssa to wire telemetry + dashboard badge, maya to own SDK spec. Assigning owners. :thumbsup:

samir: Also adding a quick acceptance test: simulate capacity pressure and assert headers emitted + telemetry event created. I'll add to routing integration tests.

alyssa: I'll add dashboard card for fallback rate and a link to quota/usage to help customers self-serve.

maya: Cool. We'll reconvene after RFC. Thanks everyone.
